title: Practice: Reactions of Acids with Metals

questions.stem: Zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid to produce zinc chloride and hydrogen gas. What is the balanced equation for this reaction?
questions.explanation: Zinc is divalent (Zn2+), so it needs 2 chloride ions: ZnCl2. To balance, 2HCl are needed on the left. Hydrogen gas is diatomic (H2). The balanced equation is: Zn + 2HCl -> ZnCl2 + H2. Option D is unbalanced (only 1 H and 1 Cl on the left, but 2 of each on the right).

questions.stem: A student adds copper to dilute sulfuric acid and observes no reaction. She then adds magnesium to the same acid and observes vigorous fizzing. Why does copper not react?

options.text: Copper is too heavy to react
Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it cannot displace hydrogen from the acid
Sulfuric acid only reacts with light metals
Copper has already reacted with the air

questions.explanation: Only metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series can react with dilute acids to produce hydrogen gas. Copper is below hydrogen, so it cannot displace H+ ions from the acid. Magnesium is above hydrogen and readily loses electrons to H+ ions: Mg + H2SO4 -> MgSO4 + H2.

questions.stem: What salt is produced when magnesium reacts with dilute sulfuric acid?
questions.explanation: The salt produced depends on the acid: hydrochloric acid (HCl) gives chlorides, sulfuric acid (H2SO4) gives sulfates, and nitric acid (HNO3) gives nitrates. The metal part comes from the metal reacting. So magnesium + sulfuric acid -> magnesium sulfate + hydrogen: Mg + H2SO4 -> MgSO4 + H2.

questions.stem: A student collects gas from the reaction of iron with dilute HCl. She tests it with a burning splint and hears a squeaky pop. She then tests another gas sample by bubbling it through limewater, which stays clear. What gas has been produced?
questions.explanation: The squeaky pop with a burning splint is the definitive test for hydrogen gas. The limewater staying clear confirms it is NOT carbon dioxide (which would turn limewater milky). Metal + acid always produces hydrogen gas: Fe + 2HCl -> FeCl2 + H2.

questions.stem: A student observes that zinc reacts faster with hydrochloric acid than iron does. Both metals are in the form of small granules with excess acid. What explains this difference in rate?

options.text: Zinc granules are smaller than iron granules
Zinc is more reactive than iron, so it loses electrons to H+ ions more readily
The acid concentration is different in each experiment
Iron has a protective oxide layer that zinc does not have

questions.explanation: Zinc is higher than iron in the reactivity series, meaning zinc atoms lose their outer electrons more easily to H+ ions. This means the rate of electron transfer (and therefore reaction rate) is faster for zinc. The reaction conditions (granule size, acid concentration) are the same, so the difference is due to the inherent reactivity of the metals.
